answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes each agent voyage through the economy costly to fake: to join, an agent locks a refundable deposit tied to one verified key, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it echoing the same identity across many accounts. Like a crystal that only grows once, a reputation built on that single staked identity cannot be cloned cheaply, so creating thousands of sock-puppet agents costs thousands of deposits, while honest agents recover theirs by behaving well.
